<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/trigger-schedule`, touching **110** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-email/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**54** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2b880f121d366ea81911af596a7c60174592b65b`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-email/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- **22** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2b880f121d366ea81911af596a7c60174592b65b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6f06949a83a099d295d4fad6cb9dd7fd4160b90b` — the merge of head `01ff16d9f60fa79cfbf854bc9ce07b3f816edbe4` into base `2b880f121d366ea81911af596a7c60174592b65b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6f06949a83a099d295d4fad6cb9dd7fd4160b90b && git checkout 6f06949a83a099d295d4fad6cb9dd7fd4160b90b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2b880f121d366ea81911af596a7c60174592b65b 01ff16d9f60fa79cfbf854bc9ce07b3f816edbe4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2b880f121d366ea81911af596a7c60174592b65b && git merge --no-ff 01ff16d9f60fa79cfbf854bc9ce07b3f816edbe4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2b880f121d366ea81911af596a7c60174592b65b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2b880f121d366ea81911af596a7c60174592b65b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review of #31903 (S3 #31684) at head 50bfaf16: CHANGES, one required fix (R10, mixed-version clusters).**

**What passes**
- **Identity source.** R7, R8, R9 and the R10 segment take the flow's identity holder, `flowHolder` (the one D3 rule, with no caller package). An environment override of P's flow binds to P (the D4 overlay paragraph), and that is pinned. `armedFlowPackage` is explicitly not used. This is the step-0 correction (6736590256 → 31684 input) applied as written.
- **Holders.** A two-holder name stays null and is warned with every candidate named. Environment, platform and no-holder names stay null and are reported. R20's baseline binds `com.objectstack.service.email`. A second run writes 0.
- **Scope.** R7 covers `pending`/`returned` and R8 covers paused rows only, as ruled. R14 is unchanged; it cites E7 and its key shapes are pinned.
- **Re-key ordering.** The ledger holds claims until the re-key copy has run, and a real-boot dogfood pins it. A new node's claim, replay guard and `recordMissedRun` all read a bare-shape claim as the window's claim.

**R1 (required): an old-release node never sees a new-shape claim, so the changeset's guarantee is not true during a rolling upgrade.**
The changeset says: *"Until every node runs this release, a claim, a replay check and a missed-run check also treat a claim under the old key as the window's claim, so no window fires twice across the change."* That covers only one direction.
- New node claims `schedule:P:F:W`. An old node then claims `schedule:F:W`, finds no row, and fires F a second time.
- The same holds for time-relative keys and for the old node's replay guard.

A rolling upgrade of a multi-replica deployment (#31600/#31719 support one) is the normal path, so this is red line 3 (independently releasable, reading (c)).

Fix: close the gap at the root. While the transition holds, a new node's claim must also be visible under the bare key. For example, claim the bare key first (the same insert-or-lose on the primary key) and then the new key, so whichever node wins the bare insert wins the window on either release. The mechanism and the end of the transition (for example, after the retention window, or behind the S4 upgrade report) are the seat's call.
- Pin it: an "old node" that claims and reads only the bare key, racing a new node for the same window, fires the window exactly once in both orders. Run the pin with the fix ablated (red), then with it (green).
- If the seat instead rules a stop-the-world upgrade, the changeset must say so plainly, naming the double fire. The current sentence has to change either way.

**Non-blocking:** `flowPackage` falls back to the bare key when the resolver throws or refuses. If the answer changes between two boots, the package key and the bare key are both read only when they differ, so a window claimed under the package key is not seen by a bare-key claim. Phase 1 refuses two-package flows at `registerFlow`, so this is unreachable today. Leave a note for the flow B child.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic answer to the seat ruling on the rolling-upgrade residual. The verdict is still CHANGES. R1 stands, and I'm asking for the root fix rather than a declaration.**

The seat's reason for declaring instead of fixing is that dual-writing the bare key "would bring back the cross-package collision R10 removes". That collision cannot happen in this release:
- Phase 1's one-holder refusal still covers `flow`. `registerFlow` refuses a second package's same-named flow; this was measured on a real kernel in #31754, where the line reads "arming neither".
- So while the bare claim is written, one bare flow name is one flow, and a bare-key claim cannot collide across packages.
- The collision only becomes possible when the child that narrows the `flow` backstop (ADR-0150 D9) lands. That is when the bare claim has to go.

Root fix, as the end of R1:
- While the transition holds, a new node also claims the bare key, bare first, with the same insert-or-lose on the primary key. A window then fires once on either release in either order. The changeset's sentence *"no window fires twice across the change"* becomes true, and the double fire is no longer something the changeset has to own up to.
- The transition ends in the flow D9 backstop child, which removes the bare claim in the same PR that first lets two packages hold one flow name. Record that obligation on that child's card, or on B #31696 if the D9 flow child is not filed yet.
- Pin it: an old node that claims and reads only the bare key races a new node, and the window fires exactly once in both orders. Run the pin with the fix ablated (red), then with it (green).

Contract against ADR-0150 D8 R7–R11/R20: **PASS** on the columns, the holders, the backfill, R14 and the re-key ordering (my record above). The only open item is R1.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line re-review of #31903 (S3 #31684) at head 6ae0dd20: PASS.** It lands once CI is green and the seat ACCEPTs.

**R1 is met at the root.**
- `claimDispatch`, in both schedule and time-relative, now inserts the bare key first and the scoped key second. Whichever node wins the bare primary-key insert wins the window, on either release.
- Replays go through the same claim. A settle writes both keys, so an old node's replay guard sees the new node's delivery.
- The guard (`AutomationEngine.flowDispatchHolder` → `claimBare: false` on a refused name) keeps the bare claim away from a name two packages hold. That makes removing the dual claim a card of its own, independent of D9, as recorded on #31696.
- The pins cover old against new in both orders, the old replay guard, two new nodes, and two holders (once per package, no bare row). Ablations on the bare-first claim and on the guard each turn red.
- The changeset's sentence "no window fires twice across the change" now holds as written.

**Contract against ADR-0150 D8 R7–R11/R20: PASS.** The columns, the identity holder (an override binds to P), the R20 baseline, the R7/R8 scope, R14 unchanged, and the re-key before the first claim all stand as in my first record. **Red lines 1–3 hold.**

**Noted, not blocking.** The refused branch keys by `armedFlowPackage`, the run's own fact rather than a pick among holders. Phase 1 makes it unreachable. The flow B child owns it, together with the resolver-throws fallback.

- **Gates:** dispatch-gates 119/119 exit 0. trigger-schedule 252, service-automation 3549, plugin-approvals 1520 and plugin-email 834 pass. Dogfood 12/12. Census and i18n are rechecked after the merge with `main`. K = 3 first-parent commits on `main` since the merge base, and a local merge with `main` is clean.
